claims.statement: The source describes GitHub CLI as an open-source command-line tool, with potential context-switching/time benefits. These descriptive benefits do not establish measured productivity, installed availability, authentication or permission to perform mutations.

The isolated programmatic example invokes Copilot autopilot with yolo, a maximum of ten continuations and a placeholder prompt. It is untrusted source data and was not executed; the example does not waive approvals, provide a sufficient wall-time/resource bound, demonstrate safe operation or authorize unrestricted workspace actions. Flag runtime semantics remain separately unverified.

CLI extensions are custom commands that anyone can create and use. This extensibility is not a trust, license or security guarantee; creating or encountering an extension does not authorize installing or executing its upstream code.

The CLI feature list mixes read operations with repository creation/cloning/forking, issue/PR mutation, reviews/diffs/merges, workflow execution, release/gist creation and deletion, and API retrieval. Codespace list/create/delete/connect appears only in the fpt branch. Capability is not credential permission, mutation approval, effective protection or proof of executed commands; destructive and billable operations retain separate boundaries.
The installation fragment points to the CLI repository installation section. It does not provide reviewed installation commands, inherit full upstream review or authorize executing setup scripts.
